conflicts.fact: Flame colour of chlorine isotopes / chlorine's flame colour
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 model-building has students write that both Cl isotopes 'would glow green in a flame test (copper-like)'. Lesson 4 says seawater burns with 'only one characteristic chlorine-family colour' and never assigns chlorine a green flame; Lesson 5's own conclusion is that flame colour is a fingerprint of atomic number, and the copper-like green claim attributes copper's colour to chlorine.

conflicts.fact: Which substance produces the violet flame
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 attributes the violet flame to potassium permanganate (a manganese compound) in the demonstration, while the story and Lessons 3, 6, 8, 9 say potassium gives violet. Lesson 1 also says the colour is 'linked to the identity of the substance rather than the colour of the solution', yet the permanganate solution is itself purple.

conflicts.fact: Hydrogen classified as a Group 1 element with Li, Na, K sharing lone ns¹
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 lists Group 1 as H, Li, Na, K in the colour-coding and Observed section, but the Overview and predict task name Group 1 metals as Li, Na, K. Hydrogen is not a Group 1 metal, so the group membership is inconsistent within the sequence.

conflicts.fact: Atom of the model drawn / which lesson revises the Lesson 1 drawing
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the initial drawing will be revised at the end of Lesson 3 (Bohr) and Lesson 7 (orbital model) and looked at again in Lesson 9, but Lesson 6 introduces the orbital model and Lesson 7 covers filling rules; Lesson 8 calls the model booklet 'your sodium diagram from Lesson 4', although sodium diagrams were first drawn in Lesson 3 or 6.

conflicts.fact: Shell capacity notation and Lesson 3's shell rule
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 states shell capacities as 2, 8, 8… and drawings only for elements 1–10, but also writes arrangements for elements 11–15; Lesson 2 uses elements 1–20 cards. Lesson 3's Observed says elements 11–15 notation is practised while Part B covers only elements 1–10.

conflicts.fact: Model building history in Lesson 6's account of the cumulative model
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says nucleus composition was added in Lessons 4–5, while Lessons 4 and 5 state they added isotopes and RAM layers (not the nuclear composition), and Lesson 2 already included the nucleus.
